sentences.text:
Neerendra Singh Parihar vs The Collector/Additional Collector
on 7 October, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:50615
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Jabalpur
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Deepak Khot
 On The 7 th Of October, 2025
 Misc. Petition No. 1621 of 2022
 Neerendra Singh Parihar
 Versus
 The Collector/Additional Collector And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Bhagwan Singh Thakur - Advocate for the petition
 Shri S.M. Guru - Assistant Solicitor General with Ms.
 Patel - Advocate for the respondent/Railways.
 Shri Mukund Agrawal and Shri Praveen Namdeo - Governm
 Advocates for the State.

Order 
The present petition has been filed by the petitioner challenging the order dated 28.03.2022 (Annexure P/1), whereby, the Additional Collector exercising revisional jurisdiction has dismissed the revision filed by the petitioner against order dated 11.10.2021, by which the SDO, Nagod has accorded sanction in Case No.528A/2020-21 to review the order dated 09.12.2020 (Annexure P/11).
2. It has been contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the order dated 11.10.2021 passed by the SDO is without jurisdiction.
It is further submitted that as per Section 51 of the MPLRC, only District Collector or District Survey Officer can accord sanction to review the order.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50615 2 MP-1621-2022
On the basis, prayed for quashment of the order dated 28.03.2022 (Annexure P/1).
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the State submitted that the SDO has the authority to accord the sanction for review the order passed by the Tehsildar.

It is submitted that the petitioner whose land has been acquired for laying railway track has got the endorsement done of his diverted land and construction in column No.12 by the orders of the Tehsildar vide (Annexure P/11) dated 09.12.2020.

Such an order was against the award passed in Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (For brevity 'Act, 2013), which was initiated vide notification dated 06.08.2020 (Annexure RJ-1).

sentences.text: It is the case of the respondents that under the garb of the order dated 09.12.2020 (Annexure P/11), the petitioner had constructed over the Survey No.934/1 which is under notification for acquisition and the award has been passed, therefore, the authorities have decided to review the order passed by the Tehsildar dated 09.12.2020 (Annexure P/11) and sought permission from the concerning SDO which has been accorded vide order dated 11.10.2021 (at page 56) of the petition.
However, on perusal of the provision of review, the counsel has submitted this permission was required to be given by the Collector, which has been accorded by the SDO.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

It is evident from the order dated 11.10.2021 that the matter was NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50615 3 MP-1621-2022 placed before the Tehsildar for sanction to review the order dated 09.12.2020 Anneuxre P/11 and same has been granted.

However, this sanction is against the mandate of Section 51 of the MPLRC, wherein the sanction could have been granted either by the District Collector or District Survey Officer to whom Tehsildar is immediately subordinate.

7. In the wake of the factual backdrop of the case as well as the provisions of law, this Court is of the considered opinion that the order passed by the SDO dated 11.10.2021 is without jurisdiction and is hereby quashed.
Accordingly, the order passed in revision petition filed against the said order dated 28.03.2022 (Annexure P/1) is also quashed.

However, it is directed that the matter be placed before the Collector for grant of sanction to review the order dated 09.12.2020 in the light of notification dated 06.08.2020 (Annexure RJ-1) and award dated 05.08.2021.
8.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the respondents that because of the status quo granted by this Court, the project of laying railway track has been stalled from 2022, therefore, the petitioner is directed to appear before the Collector on 14.10.2025.
The Collector is expected to decide the matter of sanction within seven days from the date of appearance of the parties.

9. Accordingly, the review proceedings be initiated by giving opportunity to all the stakeholders in the matter and entire proceeding be completed within one month from the date of receipt of the order of the sanction, in accordance with law.

10. As it is found by this Court that the present petition is only in respect of the irregularities committed by the review authority in regard to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50615 4 MP-1621-2022 initiation of the review proceedings, therefore, if the land of the petitioner has already been acquired under the Act, 2013, for laying railway track, then respondent authority shall be free to lay such line without any further delay as the project is in the interest of public at large.

11. Accordingly, the Petition is disposed of in above terms.
12.
All pending interlocutory applications stand disposed of.
